title: Define and scaffold the initial monorepo
milestone: M0 — Open-source foundation
body:
## Goal
Create the agreed top-level application, service, package, integration and infrastructure directories with minimal build tooling.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Repository structure matches or updates `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- [ ] Each workspace has an ownership and license note
- [ ] A fresh checkout can run documentation checks
- [ ] No framework choice is hidden; accepted decisions are recorded in an ADR

title: Implement first-run installation and household onboarding
milestone: M1 — Multi-user messages and shared display
body:
## Goal
Create the guided first-run flow described in `docs/FIRST_RUN_SETUP.md`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Installation owner is claimed securely
- [ ] First household and several people can be created
- [ ] Age group is optional and full birth date is not required
- [ ] Users can choose English or Norwegian Bokmål
- [ ] Integrations are optional and skippable
- [ ] Test message verifies the first display

title: Design multi-user roles, capabilities and shared-display projections
milestone: M1 — Multi-user messages and shared display
body:
## Goal
Implement server-enforced household, membership, capability and display boundaries.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Person profiles and user accounts are separate
- [ ] Role templates map to explicit capabilities
- [ ] Display clients receive only an authorized projection
- [ ] Cross-user and cross-household authorization tests exist
- [ ] Audit events cover permission and pairing changes

title: Build immediate and scheduled household messages
milestone: M1 — Multi-user messages and shared display
body:
## Goal
Let household members publish now or schedule a message for selected people and displays.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Create, preview, schedule, edit and withdraw
- [ ] Start and expiry times use household time zone correctly
- [ ] Child capabilities can allow direct publishing or approval
- [ ] Device-displayed state is not mislabelled as read
- [ ] The feature works without AI

title: Prototype shared display pairing and live updates
milestone: M1 — Multi-user messages and shared display
body:
## Goal
Create a restricted shared web display with secure pairing and live notice/message updates.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Short-lived pairing code
- [ ] Revocable display credential
- [ ] Distance-readable layout
- [ ] Live updates without manual refresh
- [ ] Stale/offline indication
- [ ] Light and dark appearance

title: Prototype Action Board and Timeline/Person Columns designs
milestone: M1 — Multi-user messages and shared display
body:
## Goal
Turn design concepts 2 and 5 into interactive prototypes across iPhone, shared display and Shelly-size layouts.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fictional data only
- [ ] Light and dark variants
- [ ] English and Norwegian text-expansion checks
- [ ] Distance readability test for shared display
- [ ] Child and adult feedback documented
- [ ] Recommendation for the first production component set

title: Define durable AI task, run and notice contracts
milestone: M2 — Durable AI tasks and notification engine
body:
## Goal
Version the schemas for task drafts, confirmed tasks, runs, source evidence, AI output, notices and deliveries.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Natural-language draft is separate from confirmation
- [ ] AI provider is not embedded in the domain model
- [ ] Source, uncertainty and run history are represented
- [ ] Delivery channels are idempotent and retryable
- [ ] Example payloads validate against schemas

title: Implement website and PDF source monitoring with deterministic change detection
milestone: M2 — Durable AI tasks and notification engine
body:
## Goal
Monitor a configured page and discovered documents while avoiding unnecessary AI calls.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fetch schedule and retry policy
- [ ] URL/document fingerprints
- [ ] New versus changed source distinction
- [ ] Original source metadata retained
- [ ] Safe parsing limits and prompt-injection threat review
- [ ] Synthetic test fixture for a changing weekly plan

title: Create provider-neutral structured AI extraction
milestone: M2 — Durable AI tasks and notification engine
body:
## Goal
Extract confirmed activities, dates and things to bring using a strict validated schema.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Cloud and local provider interface
- [ ] Per-household data-egress policy
- [ ] Schema validation and unsupported-claim rejection
- [ ] Source evidence references
- [ ] Model/provider/cost metadata where available
- [ ] No guessed missing dates in tests

title: Build generic webhook ingestion and event normalization
milestone: M2 — Durable AI tasks and notification engine
body:
## Goal
Allow Codex, GitHub, Axentra, Uptime Kuma and custom scripts to publish signed events into Samvev.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Scoped webhook credential
- [ ] Signature and replay protection
- [ ] Versioned event payload
- [ ] Rate limiting and duplicate handling
- [ ] Test examples without private infrastructure data

title: Implement Homey notification and allowlisted Flow adapter
milestone: M2 — Durable AI tasks and notification engine
body:
## Goal
Use Homey for outbound notifications, inbound events and explicitly allowed Flow actions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Supported connection method is documented and tested
- [ ] User selects capabilities and Flows
- [ ] Synthetic test notification
- [ ] Errors and last successful delivery are visible
- [ ] Safety-sensitive Flows require policy/confirmation
- [ ] Tokens never reach shared displays or client logs

title: Run the class 1A weekly-plan end-to-end pilot
milestone: M2 — Durable AI tasks and notification engine
body:
## Goal
Validate the complete source-to-display loop using anonymized or synthetic weekly-plan content before any real household source is connected.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Natural-language task draft and confirmation
- [ ] New/changed document detection
- [ ] Structured relevant-item extraction
- [ ] Shared-display notice with source
- [ ] Homey delivery
- [ ] Morning briefing update rather than notification spam
- [ ] Failure and uncertainty are visible

title: Create native iPhone app shell and authentication flow
milestone: M3 — iPhone, widgets and compact displays
body:
## Goal
Create the native iPhone foundation for personal overview, tasks and messages.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] MPL-2.0 directory/license boundary confirmed
- [ ] Sign-in and household selection
- [ ] Overview, Tasks, Messages and More navigation
- [ ] Deep-link routing
- [ ] English and Norwegian Bokmål
- [ ] Light, dark and system appearance

title: Implement Next, Remember Today and Household widgets
milestone: M3 — iPhone, widgets and compact displays
body:
## Goal
Provide configurable home-screen widgets backed by an authorized snapshot.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Three widget configurations
- [ ] Household/person/privacy selection
- [ ] Deep links to exact content
- [ ] Stale state
- [ ] No reliance on widgets for urgent delivery
- [ ] Light/dark previews

title: Validate Samvev on Shelly Wall Display XL hardware
milestone: M3 — iPhone, widgets and compact displays
body:
## Goal
Determine the reliable rendering, authentication and interaction path on real Shelly Wall Display XL hardware.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Record model and firmware
- [ ] Test web/kiosk or supported alternative
- [ ] Test session persistence and touch behavior
- [ ] Measure readable density and performance
- [ ] Document limitations without assuming X2 behavior
- [ ] Produce a compact prototype recommendation

title: Implement share-sheet import from Google Keep and other apps
milestone: M4 — Calendars and household integrations
body:
## Goal
Let users share text, URLs and supported attachments into Samvev as a message, note, task or task source.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Preview and choose audience
- [ ] Clearly label import as a copy
- [ ] Preserve original content and import time
- [ ] No automatic AI use
- [ ] Test with Google Keep and at least one other iOS app

title: Design calendar aggregation and curated household output
milestone: M4 — Calendars and household integrations
body:
## Goal
Aggregate Google, Microsoft and ICS sources while preserving source ownership and household privacy.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Source events are not blindly duplicated
- [ ] Busy-only publication is supported
- [ ] Curated household calendar output is designed
- [ ] Source updates and deletions reconcile safely
- [ ] Per-calendar AI and display permissions
- [ ] Sports-calendar use case included

title: Research supported Spond integration paths
milestone: M4 — Calendars and household integrations
body:
## Goal
Determine what Spond data can be integrated through current supported mechanisms.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Primary documentation reviewed
- [ ] Calendar-only and richer-data paths separated
- [ ] Authentication and policy constraints documented
- [ ] No scraping dependency proposed as core
- [ ] Clear supported MVP recommendation

title: Build assigned and claimable household task MVP
milestone: M5 — Household tasks and rewards
body:
## Goal
Allow children and adults to claim tasks, report completion and contribute to rewards.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Assigned, exclusive claimable and collaborative task types
- [ ] Atomic claim behavior
- [ ] Optional approval
- [ ] Individual and shared reward models
- [ ] Auditable corrections and duplicate prevention
- [ ] No default child leaderboard

title: Create self-hosted Docker Compose installation and upgrade design
milestone: M6 — Production self-hosting and managed hosting
body:
## Goal
Design a guided, supportable self-hosted deployment for non-developers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Compose services and persistent volumes documented
- [ ] Secure first-run claim
- [ ] Backup/restore and upgrade strategy
- [ ] Health checks and diagnostics
- [ ] Local-only operation documented
- [ ] No mandatory paid service
